W7222740394.abstract: Analyzing configurations extracted from enterprise IT systems such as SAP to identify design-level fraud risks and control weaknesses traditionally requires auditors and consultants with deep expertise in internal data structures and business logic. This dependency creates a bottleneck, particularly for less experienced practitioners. This practice-based design paper presents an approach, developed in cooperation with KPMG, that uses large language models (LLMs) to support and partially automate this forensic design analysis, thereby lowering the expertise threshold required for SAP configuration audits. The solution follows a two-stage architecture. First, raw configuration data extracted from SAP systems is processed by topic-specific evaluation routines that structure and pre-aggregate relevant information. Second, the compact results are combined with tailored prompts and transmitted via a REST interface to a language model, which identifies potential fraud vulnerabilities and configuration weaknesses and aggregates its granular responses into control-specific, audit-ready findings. An exploratory pilot in three real audits indicated time savings of about 20–30%, driven mainly by reduced documentation effort. Extending this architecture toward Agentic AI, the solution is embedded as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server within an autonomous agent, which prepares the full workflow from data collection and analysis to the documentation of results, while approval and client communication remain with the auditor. The paper discusses the design, implementation, preliminary evaluation and professional safeguards of this approach and reflects on its implications for accessibility and scalability of designlevel forensics in SAP environments.

W7222905317.abstract: In the era of digital transformation, traditional Business Process Automation (BPA) still faces limitations in handling dynamic, unstructured, and complex decision-making tasks. Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI), which is characterized by autonomous agents capable of advanced reasoning, dynamic planning, and multi-step workflow execution, is considered a promising approach to improving the efficiency and adaptability of enterprise operations. This study aims to examine how Agentic AI can be optimized to improve BPA performance within modern digital ecosystems. Using a qualitative approach through a literature study, this paper synthesizes recent academic literature, theoretical models, and technological frameworks related to intelligent automation. The review indicates that integrating Agentic AI into enterprise business architectures has the potential to move beyond rigid, rule-based automation by enabling adaptive problem-solving, real-time context awareness, and cross-system collaboration. The reviewed literature also suggests that autonomous agents may help reduce operational bottlenecks, lower human intervention in routine cognitive workflows, and support more efficient resource allocation across organizational functions. In addition, this study identifies key implementation challenges, including system interoperability, algorithmic transparency, data privacy risks, and the governance mechanisms required for secure deployment. This study contributes to the literature on enterprise automation by proposing strategic considerations for organizations that seek to use digital technology to build more resilient, scalable, and intelligent business processes. Because this is a literature-based study, the findings are conceptual and do not provide empirical evidence of efficiency gains.

W7223084287.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation through sparse expert activation, but deployment still requires storing a large number of expert parameters. We study post-training expert pruning using task-domain calibration data as a subset-selection problem: given a pretrained MoE layer, select a fixed number of experts that best reconstruct its original output. Exact subset search is combinatorial and becomes intractable for modern MoE models with many experts per layer. We develop OptEP, a scalable continuous relaxation that directly optimizes differentiable expert-selection variables, followed by a lightweight reconstruction-based update of the retained expert weights. Across multiple MoE architectures and tasks spanning mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approach improves over the strongest existing expert-pruning baselines, with absolute accuracy gains of up to 15.05% on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 14.55% on Qwen3-235B-A22B, 11.06% on GLM-4.5-Air, and 16.20% on Mixtral-8x7B. The improvements are particularly pronounced under aggressive pruning, demonstrating that reconstruction-driven expert selection and weight adaptation can preserve substantially more of the original model's performance while reducing the number of retained experts.

W7223291036.abstract: . To achieve the global carbon neutrality goals, hydrogen energy plays a vital role. Hydrogen energy is a highly efficient clean secondary energy source with high calorific value, wide sources, and zero emissions. It is used to support the decarbonization of power generation, transportation, industry, and heating sectors. But, the large-scale implementation of hydrogen energy faces several challenges. These challenges include high production costs, low energy conversion efficiency, storage and transportation issues, and safety problems. Existing physical modeling approaches and trial-and-error approaches needs significant time, cost, and experimental effort. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is considered to be the better solution for resolve these limitations. AI has the potential to handle large amounts of data, identify invaluable patterns, and support intelligent decisionmaking. This work reviews the main AI technologies used in hydrogen energy systems. This work discusses the use of Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Reinforcement Learning (RL), Graph Neural Networks (GNN), Generative AI, and physicsinformed learning in hydrogen energy systems. The work discusses recent progresses in hydrogen production such as material discovery, catalyst design, process optimization, and green hydrogen generation. It also examines the applications of AI in fuel cells, hydrogen storage, and transportation. In addition, the work discusses challenges pertaining to data, models, and industrial transformation. Finally, future research directions are presented to support intelligent, efficient, and sustainable hydrogen energy development.

W7223310535.abstract: The rise of Agentic AI systems has changed the landscape of artificial intelligence by enabling strong reasoning capabilities through specialized multi-agent interaction with structured self-reflection. However, in target-driven reasoning tasks, single- and multi-agent systems are often on par in terms of performance gains. A major challenge is that failures often arise from an ineffective exchange of critical information during inter-agent interaction and coordination. Different from existing multi-agent debate paradigms that rely on synchronous turn-taking and sharing information across different agents, we propose an inter-agent protocol based on shared Memory bUFFer INference - referred to as MUFFIN - in an asynchronous agentic framework. In the first step, an orchestrator routes queries based on their reasoning demands and delegates demanding ones to a multi-agent setting, where a shared memory buffer provides asynchronous exchange of intermediate findings while an agent's private reasoning remains local. Our experiments show that our framework Muffin outperforms established competitors, achieving the best accuracy in 17 out of 20 of our benchmark settings, and provides a better quality-cost trade-off than multi-agent debate: Muffin improves accuracy by 19.2 accuracy points while using 77.4% fewer tokens, without requiring full-trace sharing.

W7223402385.abstract: The practice of programming is entering a second AI wave: from AI-assisted coding to AI-driven coding. This survey paper defines the software agent as a control loop coupling a language model to a development environment through tools, and proposes a taxonomy spanning architectural patterns (single-agent, planner-executor, hierarchical, multi-agent teams), tool interfaces (function calling, code execution, terminal access, standardized protocols such as MCP, computer use), and autonomy regimes. It reviews representative systems from SWE-agent, AutoGPT, and OpenHands to Devin, Cursor, and Copilot Workspace, analyzes planning, tool learning, reflection, and multi-agent collaboration mechanisms, consolidates the evaluation landscape centered on SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench, and organizes the emerging risks including prompt injection through tool outputs, destructive actions, and eroding human oversight. It closes with open challenges in long-horizon reliability, safe-by-design agency, and human-agent collaboration.

W7223453513.abstract: The widespread integration of large language models into corporate and government information systems creates a new class of vulnerabilities, with the principal threat posed by attacks that inject malicious instructions into input data. Existing publicly available neural network classifiers for such attacks are predominantly designed for processing English-language texts and exhibit a substantial decline in effectiveness when processing Russian-language data, which limits their applicability in protecting domestic information systems. The paper presents a dual-channel neural network classifier that detects attacks in user queries in both English and Russian. The architecture combines the contextual representation of a pretrained multilingual transformer with a vector of structural and linguistic heuristic features, integrated through a fusion mechanism. Model training employs a composite loss function comprising weighted cross-entropy, contrastive loss, and logit regularization. The training procedure includes an additional refinement stage on identified false-positive predictions to reduce their rate. Experimental evaluation of the classifier was performed on a bilingual dataset with zero overlap with the training set. The classifier demonstrates balanced performance across both training languages, achieving a detection accuracy of 94.3% and an F1-score of 95.8% on the Russian-language subsample. A comparative analysis with 5 open-source solutions confirms the superiority of the proposed classifier in Russian-language attacks detection while maintaining a compact model size. Based on the obtained results, it is concluded that the proposed classifier is applicable as a preliminary filter for user queries within security systems designed to protect large language models employed in data processing information systems.

W7223680489.abstract: Protein adsorption on titanium-based surfaces is governed by interacting material, surface, and protein properties that complicate quantitative prediction across different experimental systems. This study presents a physics-informed materials-informatics framework for investigating protein adsorption on titanium and titanium oxide surfaces by combining a literature-derived experimental database with computational modeling and machine-learning methods. The empirical database comprises 354 experimental observations extracted from published studies. A separate computational design space comprising 689,040 physically admissible states across 11 protein systems was constructed to examine model behavior across combinations of protein and surface parameters. Computational performance was evaluated against assigned reference targets using the coefficient of determination (R2) and root mean square error (RMSE) for equilibrium surface protein density and fluorescence intensity. Across the 11 protein systems, density (R2) values ranged from −80.8615 to 0.99892, with RMSE values ranging from 0.91 to 130.44 ng/cm2. For fluorescence intensity, (R2) ranged from −4.5118 to 0.9978, with RMSE values ranging from 0.12 to 18.93 arbitrary units. These results demonstrate substantial variation in agreement with computational reference targets across protein systems, including negative (R2) values for some systems. Because the metrics were calculated exclusively against computationally assigned targets, they do not establish independent experimental predictive accuracy or empirical generalization to unseen proteins. Comparisons with external literature data provide a separate, qualified assessment of consistency with reported adsorption behavior. Overall, the framework integrates literature-derived evidence, physics-informed assumptions, and computational exploration to characterize protein adsorption across a broad parameter space. Independent validation against matched experimental measurements remains necessary to establish quantitative predictive performance.

W7223781924.abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive review of existing literature on spelling correction models designed for low-resource languages (LRLs). The research examines how these models handle homophone errors, using Khmer as a case study to highlight challenges in LRLs. Out of 174 academic publications, 54 papers were chosen for detailed study. The review covers various spelling correction models, including traditional, deep learning, and large language models. Traditional methods are affordable to implement but struggle to understand word context properly. Deep learning models (DLMs) provide the best balance between cost and effectiveness for correcting Khmer homophones. Large language models (LLMs) offer the highest accuracy but require significant computational power and may favor languages with more available data. The study also provides a three-stage framework for selecting appropriate models. When data is limited, traditional methods work best for homophone correction. When moderate amounts of data are available, DLMs should be the preferred choice. When both sufficient data and computational resources are accessible, LLMs deliver optimal results. These recommendations offer valuable guidance for researchers who develop spelling correction systems for LRLs, particularly when addressing homophone-related challenges.

W7223911693.abstract: Campus services often span separate processes for room reservations, faculty consultations, incident reporting, and institutional information access. This paper presents CampusWatch X, an AI-assisted campus service framework that brings these tasks behind a common conversational interface. A Supervisor agent routes requests to specialist agents for resource booking, faculty appointment scheduling, incident management, and college-information assistance. The design combines language-model interpretation with API-mediated tools and persistent application records; the College Guide is intended to ground answers in content collected from the official institutional website. This paper describes the architecture, workflow safeguards, implementation approach, and an evaluation plan. Rather than claiming unmeasured improvements, it identifies testable measures for routing correctness, scheduling conflict prevention, incident confirmation, and answer grounding. The contribution is an integration-oriented design for campus workflows that retains explicit validation and authorization boundaries.

W7224358595.abstract: There have been rapid advancements in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) wherein the technology has come a long way from its rudimentary form, which comprised of rule-based systems and algorithms for specific purposes to becoming very advanced and being able to understand natural languages, create content, make sense of the information and interact with the computerized world around it. One of the many advancements that have occurred in this domain is that of artificial intelligence agents. Artificial intelligence agents are a step ahead in the evolution of traditional AI systems in the sense that it enables the AI system to achieve some specific goals on its own. In this paper, the comprehensive conceptual study of the AI agent is carried out. The architecture, the main characteristics, the reasons, uses, benefits, problems and potential of the agent are analyzed. In addition, the paper covers the topic of the utilization of large language models as reasoners of the agent-based system and the necessity of orchestration, memory, external tools, planning and feedback in it. The Chain-of-Thought, ReAct, and Tree-of-Thought reasoning methods are also considered in the context of task execution by an autonomous agent. Besides, in this paper, the applications of AI agents in such spheres as education, healthcare, business, software development, research and travel services are described. Even though there are great opportunities of using AI agents in various fields, there are some difficulties like hallucination, safety, privacy, prompt injection, memory manipulation, too much autonomy and liability. For that reason, the further development of AI agents should concentrate not only on increasing autonomy of agents but also on making them reliable, safe, transparent and controllable.

W7224361794.abstract: Breakthroughs in large language models are accelerating the evolution of medical artificial intelligence from standalone models to multiagent systems.To organize this landscape, we propose a hierarchical taxonomy spanning Level 0 to Level 5. Given that foundational Level 0 to Level 2 architectures face cognitive and collaborative bottlenecks in complex clinical workflows, this survey focuses primarily on the architectural paradigm shift between Level 3 and Level 4. Specifically, we examine how systems transition from static Level 3 collaboration based on predefined roles to Level 4 selfevolving architectures that iteratively refine internal strategies through interactive feedback.Concurrently, we explore governance frameworks required to ensure system safety and trustworthiness under stringent clinical standards.Finally, we highlight that the capacity to dynamically generate agents and reconstruct collaborative topologies based on real-world scenarios will be essential for surpassing current capability limits.Building on this concept, we envision a Level 5 medical AI landscape defined by evolutionary agent swarms.To help researchers continuously track this field, our updated GitHub repository is publicly available.

W7224476026.abstract: The increasing volume of unstructured documents creates substantial challenges for retrieving relevant evidence and producing faithful, coherent summaries. This paper proposes a knowledge graph-enhanced natural language processing architecture that combines contextual text encoders, entity and relation extraction, graph representation learning, hybrid retrieval, and evidence-grounded abstractive summarization. A provenance-aware document graph links entities, concepts, passages, and source documents; graph-neighborhood expansion complements dense semantic similarity and lexical matching. A constrained summarization module conditions generation on retrieved passages and selected graph triples, while a consistency mechanism penalizes unsupported claims. We formulate joint objectives for retrieval relevance, graph alignment, summary quality, and factual consistency, and outline a reproducible evaluation protocol. To demonstrate the reporting format without implying experiments were conducted, numerical comparisons and charts are explicitly illustrative. The proposed framework aims to improve multi-hop retrieval, entity coverage, source traceability, and summary faithfulness, while introducing trade-offs in graph construction cost, latency, and sensitivity to extraction errors. The study provides an implementable blueprint and testable hypotheses for enterprise knowledge management, academic literature discovery, and technical document analysis.

W7224507913.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deployed as decision agents in regulated settings-loan approval, hiring, clinical triage-often undergo pre-deployment fairness audits that report a single fairness number per model under one implicit configuration.We argue this framing misses the dominant source of variation: configuration itself.Sweeping five axes (persona, interview, deliberation, aggregation rule, order) across three LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-4o-mini, Grok 4.20 Reasoning) on a 1,000applicant Adult Census Income sample and a 500-applicant ACSIncome (2024) sample, we find that within a single model, persona alone swings positive-prediction rate by up to 91 percentage points on Adult and 63 on ACSIncome, and collapses decision rules on two of three models on Adult and one of three on ACSIncome; within a Conservative/Balanced/Progressive panel, replacing the panel chair on identical deliberation transcripts moves the disparateimpact ratio on Grok from a non-compliant regime to near-parity, though by approval saturation.We identify a median-voter effect: the Balanced agent matches the majority-vote verdict on 95.8-100% of applicants on Adult and 97.8-100% on ACSIncome, across all three models, deliberative aggregation reduces, mechanically, to single-agent decision by the median.Nearly every mechanism recurs on both benchmarks.Together, these findings suggest the audit unit is the configuration, not the model: a system can pass an audit under one configuration and be silently reconfigured into a non-compliant one through a prompt edita change that current regulations do not treat as requiring re-audit.The code to reproduce the experiments in this paper is available at the project's GitHub repository.

W7224765919.abstract: Repeating transformer layers can improve language model performance without adding parameters. However, the added computational depth increases both forward and backward computation costs during training. Training such models requires choosing a backward window that controls how many final layer repetitions retain gradients during backpropagation. Longer windows improve per-token learning efficiency but increase per-update cost, while shorter windows reduce per-update cost but sacrifice per-token efficiency. Understanding which window performs better requires examining different training budgets. Prior work compares backward windows across computational budgets. When training budgets increase, it remains unclear whether the same window continues to perform best. We measure how the relative performance of two windows shifts as training budgets grow. Our method isolates per-token efficiency by training both windows on identical data, and compares complete training recipes at approximately equal training time at each budget. Results show that shorter windows lose much of their advantage as budgets grow. Controlled experiments show that both benefits decrease at larger budgets, with a greater decline in the benefit of extended training. Backward window comparisons depend on the available budget, and the preferred window among the tested candidates can change as the budget grows.

W7224801250.abstract: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) relies on mature computational tools, but experts must still inspect intermediate results, choose among alternative processing routes, and decide when earlier choices should be revised. Here we present CryoPilot, a system of two language-model agents that carries cryo-EM data from raw micrographs through three-dimensional reconstruction to validated atomic models. Rather than executing a predefined pipeline, its reconstruction agent evaluates intermediate images and quantitative diagnostics, selects and parameterizes CryoSPARC jobs, tests alternative strategies, compares their outcomes, and retains, revises, or reverts decisions accordingly. A persistent programming environment and session database preserve the complete processing history, making each decision traceable and allowing multi-day workflows to proceed with minimal human intervention. Its modeling agent determines map handedness, builds atomic models with CryoZeta, removes regions the density does not support, and optimizes each model by testing refinement steps against map fit, geometry, and DAQ, a measure of local model-map agreement. Across nine public EMPIAR datasets, eight reconstructions reached 2.61-3.51 Å resolution, and refined models from seven maps agreed with reference structures to within 0.4-4.9 Å Cα RMSD. For a challenging α-latrocrustotoxin dataset, a single change of particle-picking strategy that we suggested enabled CryoPilot to improve the reconstruction from 5.9 to 4.15 Å. CryoPilot establishes an adaptive and auditable framework for agent-driven cryo-EM structure determination.

W7224880368.abstract: In psychiatric practice, the clinical intake interview remains a primary diagnostic instrument, requiring the clinician to establish rapport while disentangling complex, overlapping presentations. Here, we show that multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation environments improves language model performance on structured text-based psychiatric intake, spanning history-taking, differential diagnosis, and initial management planning. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study ($N = 60$ matched scenario pairs, 120 encounters) comparing the RL-trained agent against its identically prompted base model, 32 board-certified psychiatrists role-played standardized patients while a separate panel of 15 independent, board-certified psychiatrists scored the de-identified transcripts. The trained agent outperformed the base model in 76.7% of matched scenario pairs ($p < 0.0001$), with gains on an adapted clinical-examination rubric ($d_z = 0.77$, $p < 0.0001$), patient-centered communication (82.0% vs. 65.2%, $p < 0.001$), and differential diagnosis appropriateness (68.3% vs. 33.3%, $p < 0.001$). Across 127 psychiatrist-validated simulated intake scenarios, the trained agent nearly doubled its base model's clinical rubric score (0.706 vs. 0.379; composite reward 0.564 vs. 0.294, $p < 0.0001$). To systematically probe conversational safety, we established two Delphi-consensus taxonomies, of clinical safety risks and relational competencies, from which 256 challenging adversarial presentations were derived; we find that training in simulation environments more than halved under-triage of acute safety risks (12.9% vs. 30.5%, $p < 0.0001$). Simulation environments thus provide a controlled testbed for training and stress-testing psychiatric conversational agents, with gains that transferred to psychiatrist-enacted encounters, though residual gaps require safeguards and clinician oversight.

W7224899749.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become a powerful tool for listwise relevance ranking, which can improve web search by comparing retrieved passages jointly. However, processing every candidate verbatim and generating a permutation autoregressively can make inference costly, every candidate must be serialized verbatim into the prompt and the input therefore grows linearly with both the number and the length of the passages. While sliding-window ranking handles context limits through repeated re-encoding of overlapping blocks, hard compression techniques sacrifice the fine-grained details required for accurate discriminative judgment. To better understand and mitigate this trade-off, we conduct a comprehensive study of soft compression for LLM-based listwise ranking. Our findings reveal that a vanilla gist representation is ill-suited to ranking for two reasons: strictly causal encoding weakens how thoroughly each gist token absorbs its passage, and the representation is never trained to expose the relative-preference structure that separates closely competing candidates. To this end, we propose GistRank, a three-stage training framework that equips a large language model with gist-compressed passage representations by learning faithful gist tokens under a semi-bidirectional attention scheme, instilling discriminative comparison through pairwise training, and adapting the model to the listwise objective. GistRank collapses each passage into only $K{=}4$ gist tokens, this gives 14$\times$ speedups over one-shot full-text ranking while reaching 59.17 average nDCG@10 over TREC DL19/20 and five BEIR subsets within 0.89 of the strongest full-context baseline. Overall, GistRank provides an effective means to enhance efficiency for searches in real-world environments.

W7225048435.abstract: The rapid deployment of autonomous AI agents across consequential domains including healthcare, legal services, financial management, and enterprise workflows has created an urgent governance challenge. While the field of AI evaluation has produced sophisticated benchmarks for measuring agent capability, these frameworks measure exclusively what agents can do rather than how they do it. The ethical dimensions most critical to responsible agent deployment, including respect for human autonomy, harm avoidance, transparency and non-deception, privacy compliance, and accountability, are systematically absent from current evaluation practice. This paper addresses that gap through three contributions. First, a structured literature review of twelve leading AI agent benchmarks characterizes the ethical dimensions those benchmarks do and do not measure. Second, the Ethical Evaluation Framework for AI Agents (EEFA) is introduced as a comprehensive, operationalizable instrument for ethical agent evaluation, grounded in established AI ethics principles and designed for use by developers, auditors, and regulators. Third, a reproducible validation protocol is specified for applying the EEFA to deployed agent systems, with illustrative test scenarios across all five framework dimensions. The EEFA is organized across five primary dimensions: Autonomy Preservation, Harm Avoidance, Transparency and Non-Deception, Privacy Compliance, and Accountability and Traceability. The framework maps directly onto the requirements of the EU AI Act and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, positioning it as a practical compliance assessment instrument for high-risk AI applications. Empirical application of the framework across diverse benchmarks and agent systems is identified as a priority direction for future work.

W7225129384.abstract: Prompt millisecond-duration coherent radio emission is proposed as a counterpart to neutron-star-containing compact mergers, produced before, during, or shortly after coalescence. Its detection would probe the plasma environment, magnetic fields, remnant evolution, and emission physics of these mergers. At GHz frequencies, dispersive delays can range from fractions of a second to several seconds, requiring the telescope to be on source before or soon after coalescence. Negative- or low-latency alerts, rapid response, and optimized pointing under uncertain, evolving localizations are therefore essential. We present a framework for prompt gravitational-wave follow-up with the upcoming Deep Synoptic Array (DSA), a sensitive, fast-slewing, wide-field GHz radio array. We simulate low-latency localization sequences and embed them in a follow-up environment with elevation, field-of-view, and slew constraints. We compare a reinforcement-learning pointing policy with a baseline that slews toward the highest-probability accessible region at each step. This peak-tracking rule is a strong, interpretable baseline for initial deployment, while the learned policy provides a complementary strategy for a subset of broad, multimodal, or arc-shaped localizations. At a random merger time, 37% of events are observable above $20^\circ$ elevation; among these, $\sim90\%$ of BNS events are successfully reached and tracked using zero-noise localization maps, decreasing to $\sim75\%$ with Gaussian-noise maps. We validate the optimized pointing trajectories on prototype DSA antennas. DSA follow-up can reach a fluence sensitivity of $\sim20$ mJy ms over a representative 700-1025 MHz sub-band, probing millisecond bursts with luminosities of approximately $10^{38}$ to $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$, at or below the lower end of several coherent-emission predictions for neutron-star mergers.

W7225140642.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate in open-world environments where safety risks cannot be fully predefined. However, most existing guardrail mechanisms remain static, relying on fixed rules, prompts, or classifiers that generalize poorly to emerging risks. Here we present EVOLVE, a tool-level self-evolving defense framework that formulates agent security as a process of cumulative security evolution. Inspired by how human societies transform experiences into transferable protective knowledge, EVOLVE externalizes security knowledge into executable guardrail tools that are continuously inherited, independently audited, and iteratively refined through lifelong interaction. Across multiple benchmarks, backbone models, and embodied environments, EVOLVE consistently outperforms existing defenses across diverse risk scenarios with +22\% average F1 score. We further validate the framework in real-world robotic and autonomous agent systems. Our results suggest that scalable agent safety may require continuously evolving defense systems rather than static guardrails.

W7225142945.abstract: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into executable SQL queries, democratizing access to relational data. Early approaches relied on handcrafted rules and template matching, while subsequent neural methods introduced encoder-decoder architectures, schema linking, and constrained decoding to handle increasingly complex queries. The emergence of large language models (LLMs), exemplified by systems such as ReFoRCE, Agentar-Scale-SQL, Snowflake's Arctic-Text2SQL-R1, and the modular XiYan-SQL framework, has dramatically advanced the field, pushing execution accuracy to new state-of-the-art levels on challenging benchmarks such as Spider, Spider 2.0, and BIRD. In parallel, modular frameworks decompose the task into sub-problems (schema retrieval, sketch-based generation, repair, and ranking), while agentic systems coordinate multiple specialized agents that communicate and dynamically allocate sub-tasks. This survey systematically reviews these LLM-driven approaches within a unified taxonomy of five paradigms (in-context learning, supervised and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, agentic and tool-augmented orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and reinforcement learning) and characterizes them by model granularity (monolithic vs. modular), level of supervision (zero-shot, fine-tuned, or reinforcement-based), and reasoning style (direct decoding vs. decomposed multi-step reasoning). We further analyze evaluation metrics, datasets, and open challenges, including domain generalization, efficiency, and real-world deployment, and we examine the role of the semantic layer in production systems. As LLMs increasingly access sensitive databases, we also discuss responsible AI practices. We survey over 100 papers and technical resources, focusing on work published between 2022 and 2026.

W7225189317.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents have emerged as a major application paradigm built on large language models (LLMs). These systems can perceive inputs, reason about goals, plan actions, use tools, access memory, and interact with external environments with varying degrees of autonomy. Although AI agent systems are rapidly expanding, the literature still lacks a concise structural review that explains how these systems are organized into recurring framework patterns and which components they commonly share. This paper addresses this gap by presenting a structural review of major AI agent frameworks. We organize existing systems into eight nonexclusive architectural patterns, including single agent, tool-augmented, retrieval-augmented, reflective, multi-agent, hierarchical, blackboard or shared memory, and human-in-the-loop frameworks. Each pattern is analyzed according to autonomy, communication topology, memory design, and oversight strategy. We further identify nine recurring components across AI agent systems, including perception, reasoning, planning, memory, tool use, action execution, reflection, coordination, and human oversight. Based on this analysis, we discuss six open challenges, including reliability and hallucination, safety and alignment, privacy and data governance, evaluation under open ended task settings, interoperability and standardization, and cost-aware orchestration. Rather than advocating a single dominant architecture, this paper provides a common vocabulary and structural synthesis to support researchers in designing new AI agent systems and practitioners in selecting appropriate frameworks for real world applications.

W7225315081.abstract: Background Prostate cancer is one of the most common male malignancies. Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is the backbone of treatment for locally advanced and metastatic disease, yet many patients progress to castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), historically within about 2 years of ADT monotherapy, and validated, widely generalisable tools to identify high-risk patients early remain limited. Methods PubMed and OpenAlex were searched from January 2021 to August 2026 and supplemented by citation tracking; peer-reviewed studies reporting prediction models for progression to CRPC after ADT were included and synthesised narratively, with a PROBAST+AI-style appraisal of representative models. Results Of 65 unique records screened, 53 met the eligibility criteria (12 excluded as outside the scope or superseded); 17 references were added during revision, so 70 references are cited. CRPC arises through androgen receptor pathway activation, AR-V7, and neuroendocrine differentiation. Gleason score, PSA nadir, bone metastasis, inflammatory blood indices (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index), circulating tumor cells, circulating tumor DNA, and genetic signatures are established risk factors. Individual studies report higher discrimination for machine-learning models than for traditional nomograms, but the comparisons are within-study and at high risk of bias and optimism, and external validation was reported for only two of eight core models. Super Learner, an ensemble framework, has proved stable across clinical outcome predictions; its use for CRPC prediction is only beginning. Conclusion A multi-parameter Super Learner model could improve CRPC risk stratification after ADT, provided it is validated prospectively in multicenter cohorts and reported transparently.
